title: Ashvamedhika
hook: the sacrificial horse reaches Manipura, and the young king who comes out to meet Arjuna is his own son

segments.voice: Yesterday in Ashvamedhika, a child born without breath lived, by Krishna's declaration of truth. His name is Parikshit. Did you keep your small promise? Day eight hundred seventy-one.

The horse has been set loose at last. It wanders where it likes, and Arjuna follows it with his bow, country after country, fighting the kings who challenge it. Then it walks into Manipura. Long ago, on his travels, Arjuna married a princess of this land, Chitrangada, and left a son here. That son is king now. His name is Babhruvahana. And he comes out of the city to meet the horse, not with an army but with gifts, with brahmanas, with his head bowed to his father. Today, how Arjuna takes it.
screen: `THE HORSE WANDERS.` → `IT ENTERS MANIPURA.` → `HIS SON COMES OUT WITH GIFTS.`

segments.voice: Arjuna is angry. In Ganguli's telling, he scolds his son: I've come here guarding a sacrificial horse, as a warrior, and you greet me like this? A king of your order should come out and fight. Babhruvahana stands there, humiliated. Then someone rises up out of the earth: Ulupi, the serpent princess, another of Arjuna's wives from those same travels. She tells the young king to do what his father asked. Fight him. So he does. He arms himself, and the father and son meet in battle, and the son is good. Very good. He shoots an arrow that strikes Arjuna, and Arjuna falls to the ground and does not get up. Babhruvahana, seeing what he has done, collapses too. Chitrangada runs onto the field and finds her husband dead and her son unconscious. She turns on Ulupi: this is your doing. Babhruvahana wakes and vows to fast until he dies beside his father. And then Ulupi does the second strange thing. She brings out a gem from the serpent world, a jewel that restores life, and places it on Arjuna's chest. He wakes as if from sleep. Ulupi explains. When Arjuna brought Bhishma down from behind Shikhandi, the Vasus, Bhishma's divine brothers, cursed him. Her father pleaded for him, and the answer was that the curse would end at the hands of his own son. Today it did. The fight Arjuna demanded is the one that set him free.
screen: `ARJUNA SCOLDS HIS SON` · `ULUPI: "FIGHT HIM"` · `THE SON'S ARROW FELLS THE FATHER` · then, large: `A GEM, AND AN OLD CURSE LIFTED`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably and let your breath find its pace. Bring to mind a time someone came to you with open hands and you answered with a demand, or a test, or a correction. A child, a student, a younger colleague, anyone. Breathe in and see their face as they came toward you. Breathe out and say, silently, what you might say to them now. Then let it go and just breathe. If you pray, you can hold them in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Ashvamedhika. The book where a father, following the horse, is struck down by his own son and brought back by a serpent princess's gem.
Your line: Ashvamedhika. Today, when someone younger comes to you with a gift, receive it before you test it. Day eight hundred seventy-one.

howItsDone: Arjuna's encounter with Babhruvahana is told in the Ashvamedhika Parva, and the episode is remembered in Manipur and retold in Indian theater and storytelling.

original.note: Ulupi: the serpent princess, Arjuna's wife, who urges the fight and revives him.

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm Arjuna's rebuke of Babhruvahana and Ulupi's emergence from the earth as Ganguli tells it.
Confirm the curse: the Vasus cursed Arjuna for felling Bhishma with Shikhandi before him, Ulupi's father interceded, and the curse was to end at his son's hands.
The gem is called the Sanjivana gem in some tellings; the name is left out pending confirmation.
howItsDone's mention of Manipur remembering the episode should be checked by a Keeper, or cut.
"A king of your order" glosses Arjuna's appeal to kshatriya duty.
Editor pass: removed 'out of pride' (the text frames Arjuna's demand as kshatriya duty) and the hook line telling the listener what they would guess.
Audit: read in full against Ganguli's sequence; no factual, framing or repetition problems found, no changes.
